acquisition: Storybook stories, served pages, test harnesses, live DOM and computed styles, unreachable states: drives an existing tool to a UI state and captures it without mounting components.
adjudication: Snapshot differences, pixel diffs, ignore masks, root cause versus collateral, pass/fail verdict: compares two snapshots and names the responsible component and source line.
materialization: Screenshots, pinned browser setup, remote rendering service, fonts and device settings, rendering-input hash: paints a serialized page into an image stamped with how it was produced.
normalization: Canonical tree format, content hashes, node-to-source-line mapping, component ownership of nodes: converts raw DOM captures into comparable structure without I/O.
presentation: Spacing, alignment, grouping, visual emphasis, repeated patterns in a single screen: measures layout relationships of one UI with no prior version to compare.
reach: Import graph, per-test coverage data, affected tests and stories, skipped-item list: decides which UI states a code change could reach, naming everything left out.
report: Versioned run output file, terminal summary, HTML page, pull-request comment, agent-facing tools: renders one run's results for readers without recomputing them.
retention: Reference images, baseline history, rendering-environment keys, sign-off log, change and flakiness rates: keeps past results over time and computes trends from them.
review: Approval web interface, reviewer identity, accept or reject per change, baseline replacement, upload permissions: lets a named person approve changes and update references.
runtime: In-process events, execution IDs, trace context, which elements a test touched, code paths taken: streams signals from the running application while it is alive.
stability: Loading and network idle, animations and clocks, repeated captures, nondeterministic rendering: checks whether a capture is trustworthy before anything is concluded.
